assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration in electron lenses opened sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of interfaces, defects and single atomic columns. This is a genuine invention that created a new window onto matter and underpins much of modern materials, catalysis and device physics. The impact is broad, lasting and experimentally unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical corrector design, Haider led the working implementation (TEM and later STEM versions), and Urban brought the method to materials problems and led the instrument-building collaboration. This is a natural three-person configuration. I acknowledge my own professional proximity to the field and would want the committee to weigh that openly. Whether other groups developing STEM correctors deserve equal credit is a real open question, and I cannot verify the priority details from memory.
assessment.maturity: Corrector-equipped microscopes have been routine for roughly two decades, and the results are independently reproduced everywhere. Recognition is not premature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the TEM corrector (Haider, Rose, Urban) and the STEM corrector (Krivanek and collaborators), who are not in the credited list.
Whether the committee regards this as physics rather than instrumentation that belongs to chemistry or engineering.
My own field proximity may bias my weighting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO barriers was a decisive experimental advance beyond amorphous alumina junctions. It brought coherent spin-dependent tunnelling into practical use in read heads and MRAM and followed the 2007 GMR prize. It is a clear discovery with large societal impact.
assessment.attribution: The first room-temperature, large-TMR experiments on MgO were reported almost simultaneously in 2004 by Yuasa and by Parkin, so the two experimental groups support a fair two-person prize. Butler's first-principles prediction of symmetry filtering is important, but the theory-versus-experiment balance requires care, and other predictions (e.g. Mathon and Umerski) also exist. I would propose the experimentalists, subject to the committee's reading of the historical record.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: the effect has been reproduced widely and has been in commercial devices for many years.
uncertainties: Whether the theory contribution (Butler, and independently Mathon and Umerski) should be part of the prize.
Priority between the two 2004 experimental reports is close, and I cannot independently verify the detailed chronology.
Overlap with the earlier GMR prize may lead some members to see this as an incremental follow-up.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, started the field of moire quantum matter. The experiment showed a new tunable platform for strongly correlated physics, with a very large follow-on literature.
assessment.attribution: The theory is credited to Bistritzer and MacDonald, and the decisive original experimental observation to Jarillo-Herrero's group. The prize needs the experimental discovery to be central, and the credited trio covers it. Other theorists and experimentalists (e.g. earlier twisted-bilayer theory by others, and the superconductivity and correlated-insulator papers with several co-authors) may deserve consideration, so credit allocation is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Observed in 2018 and reproduced independently by many groups, but the field is still young and the interpretation of the superconducting phase remains debated. It is reasonably mature as a discovery but arguably early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled.
Possible additional contributors to the theory of twisted-layer flat bands.
The experimental discovery is only about eight years old, so timeliness is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Three-jet events at PETRA in 1979 gave the first direct experimental evidence for the gluon, the carrier of the strong force. This is exactly the kind of original experimental discovery the prize is meant for, even if it was not the most elegant measurement. It is central to confirming QCD.
assessment.attribution: Four PETRA collaborations (TASSO, MARK-J, PLUTO, JADE) announced the result almost simultaneously, and TASSO is usually credited first. The credited trio come from TASSO and its analysis. Wu is a prominent candidate for her role in the analysis, and a woman nominee would also be welcome, but that is not a reason for inclusion. Individual attribution within large collaborations is difficult, and I would want the historical record checked in depth.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by multiple experiments and by later precision QCD studies at LEP and elsewhere. Recognition would be very late but scientifically secure.
uncertainties: Individual credit within TASSO versus the other PETRA experiments, and between experimentalists and the theorists who proposed three-jet signatures.
The long delay since 1979 raises the question of whether anyone has been overlooked.
I cannot verify precise roles from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice idea removed the main barrier to neutral-atom optical clocks, and Ye's group brought them to unprecedented stability and accuracy. These tools open the door to relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a redefinition of the second. A clear invention with demonstrated performance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the optical lattice clock concept and demonstrated it with strontium, and Ye realized very high-performance clocks, so a two-person configuration is natural. Trapped-ion clocks, which overlap with the 2012 and 2005 prizes, are outside this candidate. Contributions of others to magic wavelengths and frequency combs are partially recognised already.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: many independent labs operate lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level. The second redefinition has not yet happened, which could argue for waiting for the final application.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to wait for the redefinition of the second.
Overlap with prior frequency-comb and ion-clock recognition.
Other contributors to the early proposal and demonstration of magic-wavelength trapping.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and its experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells created the field of topological insulators. The prize criteria require verification, and the 2007 transport experiment supplied it. It fits the committee's preference for an original experiment confirming a theory.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele predicted the quantum spin Hall effect in graphene, and Molenkamp's group measured it in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The credit puzzle is that BHZ (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and Fu and Kane for 3D materials, plus the ARPES confirmations, are not within this candidate's names, so a fair prize may need a different composition. The supplied credited names support a workable three-person set but an incomplete one.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed in many materials, with long-standing impact across condensed matter physics. Some applications remain aspirational.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who proposed HgTe, from the credited names.
Distinction from the 3D topological insulator discovery and the 2016 prize on topological phases.
Whether graphene's tiny spin-orbit gap makes Kane and Mele's original material proposal weaker than the later HgTe realisation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube detected the diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and pointed to a first source, opening neutrino astronomy at energies far above the earlier prizes. It is both a new instrument at cubic-kilometre scale and a discovery with lasting importance for the origin of cosmic rays.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the conception and the collaboration, Spiering contributed to the early detector development (and the predecessor efforts), and Karle held major project roles. IceCube is a very large collaboration, and a three-name prize unavoidably omits many essential contributors, including those at AMANDA and the Baikal and other pathfinder experiments. This is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: The 2013 detection is confirmed and the 2017 and 2022 source associations are significant but still few. The field is growing quickly but the identity of most sources is unresolved, so the discovery is secure while the astrophysical interpretation is incomplete.
uncertainties: Attribution within a collaboration of hundreds, and the role of the earlier pathfinder experiments.
Whether the source associations are strong enough for the committee's 'absolutely sure' standard.
Independent confirmation from KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultrapure single-crystal hexagonal boron nitride is the substrate and encapsulant that made high-mobility graphene and other two-dimensional devices possible, enabling the fractional quantum Hall, moire and many other discoveries. It is a materials enabler of the kind I value, a tool that lets people see phenomena that were previously hidden. Its weakness is that it is an enabling technology rather than a physical discovery in itself.
assessment.attribution: Watanabe and Taniguchi at NIMS grew the crystals and supplied the field. Kim and others developed the heterostructure device methods, and Dean et al. showed the improvement in graphene mobility. A prize for the crystals alone could be seen as narrow, and it may be better to combine it with the van der Waals assembly methods. I am not sure that Philip Kim's contribution is best seen as part of this candidate.
assessment.maturity: The crystals have been used in thousands of independent experiments for more than a decade, so confirmation and impact are solid. Whether it counts as a physics discovery rather than a materials-synthesis contribution is a committee question.
uncertainties: Whether crystal growth alone meets the 'discovery or invention' criterion in physics.
Overlap with the 2010 graphene prize and with the possible heterostructure-assembly prize.
Whether to include Philip Kim, and at whose expense.
